title: Natural therapy
titleChinese: 治疗心理疾病的天然疗法
paragraphs: The great outdoors: it’s the place to head for when you’re in need of peace and quiet, open spaces, beautiful scenery and exercise. Whether a huge mountain range or a local country park, these natural areas are a perfect tonic for our stressed-out lives, and their therapeutic effect is being used more and more to treat mental health.

As an example, in the foothills of the Snowdonia National Park in the UK, specialist therapy sessions are held to help people who suffer from depression, anxiety and stress. Outdoor art-related activities are held for patients, but the setting alone has been credited with improving the mood of patients. Art psychotherapist Pamela Stanley told the BBC that there was a "growing body of evidence" to support eco-therapy.

It’s true that for most of us connecting with the natural world definitely lifts our spirits. But the mental health charity Mind says eco-therapy has been recognised as a formal type of treatment that can sometimes be prescribed to someone by a doctor. It doesn’t involve taking medication, but instead it just develops a person’s relationship with nature. This natural remedy can take on many forms, but can include doing yoga in a forest, gardening or even hugging a tree.

Evidence has shown there are many benefits of this ‘green’ therapy, including improving social contact, social and work skills and coping abilities. It’s what Dr Rachel Bragg from the University of Essex calls ‘psychological restoration’. She told the BBC’s All in the Mind programme that nature-based therapies should be part of a "toolkit" of care for patients.

One reason why getting back to nature is, well, natural, is something called biophilia, a sort of understanding or empathy with the natural world. According to environmental psychologist Birgitta Gatersleben, “the idea that nature reminds us of life, and if we (are) exposed to the natural elements, then our sort of negative feelings get almost immediately replaced with positive emotions.”

vocabulary.entry: the great outdoors /ðə ɡreɪt ˌaʊtˈdɔːz/ 户外天地；大自然
vocabulary.example: We spent the weekend exploring the great outdoors.
vocabulary.translation: 我们周末去探索了户外天地。

vocabulary.entry: tonic /ˈtɒnɪk/ n. 滋补品；良药
vocabulary.example: A walk in the fresh air is a tonic for the mind.
vocabulary.translation: 在新鲜空气中散步是心灵的良药。

vocabulary.entry: stressed-out /ˌstrest ˈaʊt/ adj. 压力过大的；极度焦虑的
vocabulary.example: She's been feeling stressed-out since starting her new job.
vocabulary.translation: 自从开始新工作，她就一直感觉压力过大。

vocabulary.entry: therapeutic /ˌθerəˈpjuːtɪk/ adj. 治疗性的；有疗效的
vocabulary.example: Many people find gardening therapeutic.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人觉得园艺有治疗效果。

vocabulary.entry: foothills /ˈfʊthɪlz/ n. 山麓；山脚
vocabulary.example: The village is located in the foothills of the Alps.
vocabulary.translation: 这个村庄位于阿尔卑斯山的山脚下。

vocabulary.entry: specialist therapy session /ˈspeʃəlɪst ˈθerəpi ˈseʃn/ 专业治疗课程
vocabulary.example: He attends weekly specialist therapy sessions for his anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 他每周参加针对焦虑症的专业治疗课程。

vocabulary.entry: depression /dɪˈpreʃn/ n. 抑郁症；抑郁
vocabulary.example: She sought help for depression from a mental health professional.
vocabulary.translation: 她向心理健康专家寻求抑郁症的帮助。

vocabulary.entry: anxiety /æŋˈzaɪəti/ n. 焦虑症；焦虑
vocabulary.example: His anxiety makes it hard for him to sleep at night.
vocabulary.translation: 他的焦虑症让他晚上难以入睡。

vocabulary.entry: setting /ˈsetɪŋ/ n. 环境；场景
vocabulary.example: The hotel's beautiful coastal setting makes it a popular destination.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店美丽的海滨环境使其成为热门目的地。

vocabulary.entry: be credited with /bi ˈkredɪtɪd wɪð/ 被认为具有；被归功于
vocabulary.example: She is credited with inventing the first practical computer mouse.
vocabulary.translation: 她被认为发明了第一个实用的电脑鼠标。

vocabulary.entry: eco-therapy /ˈiːkəʊ ˈθerəpi/ 生态疗法（利用自然环境进行的心理或生理治疗）
vocabulary.example: Eco-therapy combines nature exposure with therapeutic techniques.
vocabulary.translation: 生态疗法将接触自然与治疗技巧相结合。

vocabulary.entry: lift one's spirits /lɪft wʌnz ˈspɪrɪts/ 振奋精神；使心情好转
vocabulary.example: The good news really lifted her spirits.
vocabulary.translation: 这个好消息真的让她振奋起来。

vocabulary.entry: prescribe /prɪˈskraɪb/ v. 开具（药方）；推荐（治疗方案）
vocabulary.example: The doctor prescribed a course of physical therapy for his injury.
vocabulary.translation: 医生为他的伤势开具了物理治疗方案。

vocabulary.entry: medication /ˌmedɪˈkeɪʃn/ n. 药物；药剂
vocabulary.example: She takes medication to control her blood pressure.
vocabulary.translation: 她服用药物来控制血压。

vocabulary.entry: natural remedy /ˈnætʃrəl ˈremədi/ 自然疗法；天然药物
vocabulary.example: Honey is a popular natural remedy for sore throats.
vocabulary.translation: 蜂蜜是治疗喉咙痛的常用自然疗法。

vocabulary.entry: gardening /ˈɡɑːdnɪŋ/ n. 园艺；园艺活动
vocabulary.example: Gardening is a relaxing hobby that many people enjoy.
vocabulary.translation: 园艺是很多人喜欢的放松爱好。

vocabulary.entry: psychological restoration /ˌsaɪkəˈlɒdʒɪkl ˌrestəˈreɪʃn/ 心理修复
vocabulary.example: Spending time in nature promotes psychological restoration after stress.
vocabulary.translation: 压力过后，在自然中度过时光有助于心理修复。

vocabulary.entry: toolkit /ˈtuːlkɪt/ n. 工具箱；一套工具（此处喻指治疗手段）
vocabulary.example: Cognitive-behavioral therapy is part of the toolkit for treating anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 认知行为疗法是治疗焦虑症的手段之一。

vocabulary.entry: biophilia /ˌbaɪəˈfɪliə/ n. 热爱生命或自然的本性
vocabulary.example: Biophilia explains why people feel calm in natural surroundings.
vocabulary.translation: 亲生命性解释了为什么人们在自然环境中会感到平静。

vocabulary.entry: empathy /ˈempəθi/ n. 共情；同理心
vocabulary.example: She has great empathy for people going through difficult times.
vocabulary.translation: 她对经历困境的人抱有强烈的同理心。

vocabulary.entry: environmental psychologist /ɪnˌvaɪrənˈmentl saɪˈkɒlədʒɪst/ 环境心理学家
vocabulary.example: The environmental psychologist studies how surroundings affect mood.
vocabulary.translation: 这位环境心理学家研究环境如何影响情绪。

vocabulary.entry: natural elements /ˈnætʃrəl ˈelɪmənts/ 自然元素（如阳光、空气、水、植物等）
vocabulary.example: The design of the building incorporates natural elements like wood and stone.
vocabulary.translation: 这座建筑的设计融入了木材和石头等自然元素。

sentences.english: The great outdoors: it’s the place to head for when you’re in need of peace and quiet, open spaces, beautiful scenery and exercise.
sentences.chinese: 户外天地：当你需要内心的宁静、安静开阔的空间、美丽的风景和运动时，这里就是你的目的地。

sentences.english: Whether a huge mountain range or a local country park, these natural areas are a perfect tonic for our stressed-out lives, and their therapeutic effect is being used more and more to treat mental health.
sentences.chinese: 无论是巍峨的山脉，还是本地的郊野公园，这些自然区域都是我们压力重重生活的绝佳良药，它们的治疗效果正越来越多地被用于心理健康治疗。

sentences.english: As an example, in the foothills of the Snowdonia National Park in the UK, specialist therapy sessions are held to help people who suffer from depression, anxiety and stress.
sentences.chinese: 例如，在英国斯诺登尼亚国家公园的山脚下，专门的治疗课程被用于帮助患有抑郁症、焦虑症和承受压力的人群。

sentences.english: Outdoor art-related activities are held for patients, but the setting alone has been credited with improving the mood of patients.
sentences.chinese: 这里为患者举办与艺术相关的户外活动，但仅就环境本身而言，就被认为对改善患者情绪起到了积极作用。

sentences.english: Art psychotherapist Pamela Stanley told the BBC that there was a "growing body of evidence" to support eco-therapy.
sentences.chinese: 艺术心理治疗师帕梅拉·斯坦利向英国广播公司表示，支持生态疗法的“证据越来越多”。

sentences.english: It’s true that for most of us connecting with the natural world definitely lifts our spirits.
sentences.chinese: 诚然，对我们大多数人来说，与自然世界建立联系无疑会振奋精神。

sentences.english: But the mental health charity Mind says eco-therapy has been recognised as a formal type of treatment that can sometimes be prescribed to someone by a doctor.
sentences.chinese: 但心理健康慈善机构“心智”（Mind）表示，生态疗法已被认可为一种正式的治疗方式，医生有时会为患者开具这种治疗方案。

sentences.english: It doesn’t involve taking medication, but instead it just develops a person’s relationship with nature.
sentences.chinese: 它无需服用药物，而是通过培养人与大自然的关系来发挥作用。

sentences.english: This natural remedy can take on many forms, but can include doing yoga in a forest, gardening or even hugging a tree.
sentences.chinese: 这种自然疗法可以有多种形式，包括在森林里做瑜伽、园艺，甚至是拥抱树木。

sentences.english: Evidence has shown there are many benefits of this ‘green’ therapy, including improving social contact, social and work skills and coping abilities.
sentences.chinese: 有证据表明，这种“绿色”疗法有诸多益处，包括改善社交关系、提升社交和工作技能以及应对能力。

sentences.english: It’s what Dr Rachel Bragg from the University of Essex calls ‘psychological restoration’.
sentences.chinese: 埃塞克斯大学的雷切尔·布拉格博士将其称为“心理修复”。

sentences.english: She told the BBC’s All in the Mind programme that nature-based therapies should be part of a "toolkit" of care for patients.
sentences.chinese: 她在接受英国广播公司《心灵深处》（All in the Mind）节目采访时表示，自然疗法应成为患者护理“工具箱”的一部分。

sentences.english: One reason why getting back to nature is, well, natural, is something called biophilia, a sort of understanding or empathy with the natural world.
sentences.chinese: 回归自然之所以“自然而然”，其中一个原因是一种名为“亲生命性”（biophilia）的特质——一种对自然世界的理解或共情能力。

sentences.english: According to environmental psychologist Birgitta Gatersleben, “the idea that nature reminds us of life, and if we (are) exposed to the natural elements, then our sort of negative feelings get almost immediately replaced with positive emotions.”
sentences.chinese: 环境心理学家比吉塔·盖特斯莱本表示：“自然让我们联想到生命，当我们接触自然元素时，负面情绪几乎会立即被积极情绪所取代。”
